case_title: Sunderlal Kanaiyalal Bhatija v. State of Maharashtra
confession: Confession made by accused under TADA Act, relied on
neutral_facts: The accused was involved in a case under the TADA Act where a confessional statement was recorded and used as evidence leading to his conviction. A separate complaint was filed against him under sections 302, 307, 353, and 402 of the Indian Penal Code, along with section 35(c) of the Arms Act, 1959. The TADA Act was initially applied but later dropped as it was determined that the offences under TADA were not applicable. The confessional statement from the TADA case was sought to be used in the IPC case, but the trial court and high court rejected this. The Supreme Court held that the confessional statement could not be used in the IPC case as the charges were only under the IPC and not under TADA.
